title: FAFSA completion and college attendance association

excludedEvidence: H2 uses original graduation-cohort FAFSA proxy and is excluded.
03_correlations.csv p-values are excluded because the negative-correlation export bug is known.

existingStataAdjustedAssociation.interpretation: A 10-percentage-point higher school estimated FAFSA completion rate is associated with a 4.9-percentage-point higher college attendance rate, controlling for listed school characteristics.
controls: Student low-income share, per 10 percentage points
School type: public secondary, charter, vocational/technical, other
existingStataAdjustedAssociation.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals; standard errors clustered by district; 295 districts and residual df 294.
existingStataAdjustedAssociation.causalLimit: School-level observational association. College-going plans or other unmeasured differences can influence both FAFSA completion and college attendance. The coefficient is not an estimated effect of completing a FAFSA or of an assistance program.
existingStataAdjustedAssociation.populationLimit: FAFSA numerator is a screened Federal Student Aid count divided by October 2024 senior enrollment, not matched student records. College attendance concerns Class of 2025 graduates observed by March 2026; the two populations differ.

sameSampleBaseline.interpretation: Adding estimated FAFSA completion increases in-sample R-squared. This is descriptive fit improvement, not causal mediation or out-of-sample predictive validation.

independentValidation.method: OLS with district cluster sandwich variance and Stata finite-sample adjustment G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-K), t inference df=G-1.
